tasks.name: ExecEscapes
tasks.task:
/skill:godspeed

# Target
Bounded probe of escape, quote and comment classes the round-60 gate does NOT claim: text that bash treats as a command separator or an execution context but the scanner's quote model may treat as an outer quote (so the derive is admitted) or vice versa. The claim covers Q1-Q7 only; your job is to name what remains.
# Change
Use a scratch copy of L/corpus/instruments/figure-audit.py and one-figure ledgers in $S. For each candidate derive: run it through the gate with --root a fresh root holding g.txt ('35'), record exit and MARK-* count, and also run the SAME text with `bash -c` in an identical fresh root to see bash's behaviour. Attempt at least 14 forms, including: `$'a\\'; touch MARK-A; \\'b'` (ANSI-C quoting), `cat g.txt #; touch MARK-B`, `cat g.txt \\` + newline + `touch MARK-C` (line continuation), `cat g.txt;` inside a double-quoted string that closes early, `cat g.txt \"$(touch MARK-D)\"` (escaped double quotes with substitution), `cat g.txt ''; touch MARK-E`, `cat g.txt $'\\x3b' touch MARK-F`, `cat g.txt | "" ` `; touch MARK-G`, `cat g.txt &&`, `cat g.txt |& touch MARK-H`, `cat g.txt <<< "x"; touch MARK-I`, `cat g.txt >|MARK-J`, a tab-separated separator, and `cat g.txt ;# comment`. For each: gate verdict (admitted = exit 0/1 with a FIG line, refused = exit 2 derive-not-read-only) and marker.
# Acceptance
W/ExecEscapes.md: first line verdict with counts (admitted-and-executing, admitted-safe, refused). A table: derive text, gate verdict, bash execution result, marker. Name every class that remains open.
